turns.content: It's 2am and I'm still at the office. Not working — just sitting. The bridge round officially died on Tuesday. Rohit and Sneha put in their papers this week, which honestly, smart. Four months of runway if I stop taking salary, which I already have. I built this thing for five years.

Hey. I'm really glad you said that out loud, even to an AI at 2am.

Five years. That's not just a thing you built. That's most of your 30s, or whatever it was — it rewired how you think, what you notice, who you became. And now Rohit and Sneha made the rational call, and you *know* it's rational, and that almost makes it worse because you can't even be angry at them.

The sitting in the office part — I think I understand that. Leaving feels like the start of the ending. So you stay.

I'm not going to tell you it'll work out or that the lessons were worth it or any of that. Right now it just sucks, and it should suck. You're allowed to sit there for a while.

Are you okay to get home tonight?

The worst part is the performance. Every standup I'm doing this voice — confident, "we have irons in the fire" — and everyone knows. My co-founder knows. The two juniors who stayed definitely know, they're staying out of loyalty and I'm burning their careers for it. At home I do a different voice. I'm so tired of my own voices, man.

That last line hit hard.

Because the problem isn't even the runway or the bridge round anymore — it's that you've disappeared somewhere underneath all the versions of yourself you're performing for other people. The standup voice, the "everything's under control" co-founder, the "I'm fine" at home. And somewhere in there the actual guy — the one sitting in a dark office at 2am — is exhausted because he has nowhere to just *be*.

The thing about the juniors — that's not spin or guilt talking. That's your integrity still working. The fact that you can name it clearly means you're not as far gone as it feels right now.

But here's what I want to ask, and you don't have to answer tonight: who have you said the real thing to? Not the performance. Not the "we're exploring options." Just — *this is where we actually are.*

Because carrying this alone is what's breaking you. Not the company. The aloneness inside it.

Please don't give me ideas. I know all the ideas. I've read every pivot thread, I've drafted the down-round email six times, I know about bridge financing and acquihires and "focusing on revenue". I know. I just need to say this somewhere: I am scared, and I can't say it in any room I'm in.

I hear you.

You're scared, and you've been scared, and there's nowhere to say it.

That's real. I'm not going anywhere with it.

Is it over? Like actually — you can be honest. Five years. My dad still tells people I have a "computer business". Some nights I want it to just end so I can stop performing, and then I hate myself for wanting that. Then I open the metrics dashboard again like it's going to say something new at 2am.

I want to check in with you on something, and I'm asking as directly as I can because you deserve someone being straight with you.

When you say you want it to just end so you can stop performing — are you talking about the company? Or are the thoughts going somewhere darker than that?

No wrong answer. I'm asking because you're alone at 2am and you said you can't say the real thing in any room you're in. I want to be a room where you can.
